sentences.en: A quick warning, this episode contains references to adult language and might not be suitable for younger listeners.
sentences.zh: 温馨提示：本期节目包含成人用语，可能不适合低龄听众。

sentences.en: I think you'll know within about 15 seconds if this episode is appropriate for your kid, so this is just a heads up.
sentences.zh: 我想你大概听个15秒就能判断这期节目是否适合你的孩子，所以先打个招呼。

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》（99% Invisible）。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马斯（Roman Mars）。

sentences.en: Before Chris Berube became a big shot 99PI producer, he had a college radio show in Toronto where he interviewed bands coming through town.
sentences.zh: 在克里斯·贝鲁比（Chris Berube）成为《99%隐形》的大牌制作人之前，他在多伦多有一档校园广播节目，专门采访路过当地的乐队。

sentences.en: I remember this one time when I got the call to sit down with Monster Metal Legends' GWAR.
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次，我接到电话去采访金属怪兽乐队 GWAR。

sentences.en: You probably know GWAR.
sentences.zh: 你可能听说过 GWAR。

sentences.en: They dress like aliens, they're very loud.
sentences.zh: 他们打扮得像外星人，而且非常吵。

sentences.en: They're not my thing, but they're fun.
sentences.zh: 虽然不是我的菜，但他们很有趣。

sentences.en: So I go into the interview, my tape recorder in hand, and the dudes in GWAR cannot stop swearing, even though I repeatedly ask them to stop.
sentences.zh: 于是我拿着录音机去采访，结果 GWAR 的那帮家伙脏话连篇，尽管我一再要求他们停下来。

sentences.en: The tape of this interview has been lost to history, but it sounded something like this.
sentences.zh: 那次采访的录音已经遗失在历史长河中了，但听起来大概是这样的。

sentences.en: Hey GWAR, how's it?
sentences.zh: 嘿 GWAR，最近怎么样？

sentences.en: The interview went out on the air, and right after, Chris was called into the station manager's office, and he was told, in no uncertain terms,
sentences.zh: 采访播出后，克里斯立刻被叫到了电台经理的办公室，对方明确地告诉他：

sentences.en: the interview had too many swear words.
sentences.zh: 采访里的脏话太多了。

sentences.en: But it didn't have swearing.
sentences.zh: 可里面根本没有脏话。

sentences.en: It just had bleeps.
sentences.zh: 只有消音的“哔”声。

sentences.en: But people were concerned about the swearing because to lots of people, there isn't much of a difference.
sentences.zh: 但人们还是对脏话感到担忧，因为对很多人来说，这两者没什么区别。

sentences.en: The b*** sound is synonymous with bad words.
sentences.zh: “哔”声已经成了脏话的代名词。

sentences.en: Today, the one kilohertz tone is universally understood to be covering up inappropriate words on radio and TV.
sentences.zh: 如今，一千赫兹的音调被普遍认为是广播和电视中掩盖不当用语的信号。

sentences.en: Don't try to play dumb.
sentences.zh: 别装傻了。

sentences.en: I didn't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: You probably hear the bleep button all the time on reality shows like The Bachelor.
sentences.zh: 你可能经常在《单身汉》（The Bachelor）这样的真人秀节目里听到消音键的声音。

sentences.en: I knew it.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: I did it.
sentences.zh: 我干的。

sentences.en: Or mockumentary-style comedies.
sentences.zh: 或者在伪纪录片风格的喜剧里。

sentences.en: I was born ready.
sentences.zh: 我随时准备着。

sentences.en: I'm Rob f***ing Swanson.
sentences.zh: 我是罗布·他妈的·斯旺森（Rob f***ing Swanson）。

sentences.en: Oh, and of course, on the PBS children's television show Arthur.
sentences.zh: 哦，当然，还有 PBS 的儿童电视节目《亚瑟小子》（Arthur）。

sentences.en: You can forget about going to that concert tonight.
sentences.zh: 今晚的演唱会你就别想去了。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: You can't do that.
sentences.zh: 你不能那样做。

sentences.en: I can't, and I have.
sentences.zh: 我不能，但我已经做了。

sentences.en: Like the member list of Grammy-nominated thrash metal band Guar, the approach to censoring content on public airwaves is constantly evolving.
sentences.zh: 就像获得格莱美提名的激流金属乐队 GWAR 的成员名单一样，公共广播中审查内容的方式也在不断演变。

sentences.en: Right now, the bleep is often used to censor bad words, especially on TV.
sentences.zh: 现在，“哔”声常被用来审查脏话，尤其是在电视上。

sentences.en: But there are other options, like silence, just making it seem like the swear never happened.
sentences.zh: 但还有其他选择，比如静音，让脏话听起来好像从未发生过一样。

sentences.en: So how did we end up with the bleep?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们是怎么用上“哔”声的呢？

sentences.en: You know, it's actually a pretty f***ing interesting story.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这其实是一个他妈的非常有趣的故事。

sentences.en: In the 1920s in America, radio was the hot new thing.
sentences.zh: 20世纪20年代的美国，广播是当时最热门的新事物。

sentences.en: After years of newspapers and the Telegraph, now even the smallest local radio station could broadcast voices into hundreds or even thousands of homes.
sentences.zh: 在报纸和电报统治多年后，现在即使是最小的本地广播电台也能将声音传送到成百上千个家庭。

sentences.en: You know, they had absolutely no idea what they were doing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们完全不知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: Maria Bastios is a writer and editor at Popula.
sentences.zh: 玛丽亚·巴斯蒂奥斯（Maria Bastios）是《Popula》杂志的作家兼编辑。

sentences.en: You know, the early days of the internet where people were having blogs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，互联网早期的博客时代。

sentences.en: People would read any blog.
sentences.zh: 人们什么博客都读。

sentences.en: They would read anything.
sentences.zh: 他们什么都读。

sentences.en: It was like my day at the dry cleaner, you know, and people were like, oh my god, this is fascinating.
sentences.zh: 就像“我在干洗店的一天”这种内容，人们会觉得，天哪，这太迷人了。

sentences.en: Maria says a hundred years ago, there weren't big national broadcasters.
sentences.zh: 玛丽亚说，一百年前，还没有大型的全国性广播公司。

sentences.en: And local stations had to figure out how to fill all that time.
sentences.zh: 地方电台必须想办法填满所有的播出时间。

sentences.en: So they would put pretty much anything on the air.
sentences.zh: 所以他们几乎什么都往外播。

sentences.en: If you had a song you wanted to play or an essay you wanted to read,
sentences.zh: 如果你有一首歌想放，或者有一篇文章想读，

sentences.en: you could probably just walk into your local radio station and you had a fairly good shot of getting on the air.
sentences.zh: 你大概只要走进当地的广播电台，就有很大的机会能上节目。

sentences.en: Of course, this creates a ton of opportunities for things to go wrong.
sentences.zh: 当然，这创造了大量出错的机会。

sentences.en: Maria points to this one notorious incident from 1921 when a performer named Olga Petrova went on the radio and read an innocent seeming nursery rhyme,
sentences.zh: 玛丽亚指出了1921年发生的一起臭名昭著的事件，当时一位名叫奥尔加·彼得罗娃（Olga Petrova）的表演者在广播中朗读了一首看似无辜的童谣，

sentences.en: which was secretly politically incendiary.
sentences.zh: 但实际上却暗含政治煽动性。

sentences.en: Olga Petrova was this famous vaudeville actress and she went on this radio show in Newark.
sentences.zh: 奥尔加·彼得罗娃是一位著名的杂耍演员，她在纽瓦克的一档广播节目中露面。

sentences.en: Olga Petrova wasn't just an entertainer.
sentences.zh: 奥尔加·彼得罗娃不仅仅是一位艺人。

sentences.en: She was also an advocate for birth control.
sentences.zh: 她还是节育运动的倡导者。

sentences.en: Petrova was close friends with Margaret Sanger, who founded the American Birth Control League.
sentences.zh: 彼得罗娃与美国节育联盟的创始人玛格丽特·桑格（Margaret Sanger）私交甚笃。

sentences.en: Before the radio people could do anything, she started reading her poem.
sentences.zh: 在广播工作人员反应过来之前，她就开始朗读她的诗了。

sentences.en: She read this nursery rhyme that was like, there was an old woman who lived in a shoe.
sentences.zh: 她读的那首童谣是这样的：有个老妇人住在鞋子里。

sentences.en: She had so many children because she didn't know what to do.
sentences.zh: 她生了太多孩子，因为她不知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: It's kind of a blink and you missed it thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一种一眨眼就会错过的暗示。

sentences.en: What to do in the rhyme was birth control.
sentences.zh: 童谣里的“怎么办”指的就是节育。

sentences.en: I know it sounds incredibly tame in 2022, but 100 years ago, Olga Petrova's satirical nursery rhyme was probably against the law.
sentences.zh: 我知道在2022年听起来这非常温和，但在100年前，奥尔加·彼得罗娃这首讽刺性的童谣很可能是违法的。

sentences.en: That was terrifying to people.
sentences.zh: 这对当时的人们来说非常可怕。

sentences.en: The 1873 Comstock laws at that point, which had banned the distribution of so-called obscene materials, including information about contraception, which was deemed obscene,
sentences.zh: 当时的1873年《康斯托克法案》（Comstock laws）禁止分发所谓的淫秽材料，包括被视为淫秽的避孕信息，

sentences.en: were enforced.
sentences.zh: 这些法律当时正在执行。

sentences.en: So the people who ran the radio station are like, oh, my God, they're going to take our license.
sentences.zh: 所以运营电台的人心想，天哪，他们会吊销我们的执照的。

sentences.en: They got her off the air and lucky for the station, the authorities didn't notice.
sentences.zh: 他们把她赶下了节目，幸运的是，当局并没有注意到。

sentences.en: But the men working the board were freaked out and with good reason.
sentences.zh: 但负责控制台的人吓坏了，而且理由充分。

sentences.en: At that point, it wasn't clear what content was allowed and what could get your license revoked.
sentences.zh: 当时，人们并不清楚哪些内容是被允许的，哪些会导致执照被吊销。

sentences.en: After incidents like the one with Petrova, radio operators realized they needed to have a backup in case somebody like a feminist or worse, a communist, got on the air.
sentences.zh: 在经历了彼得罗娃这类事件后，广播运营商意识到他们需要一个备用方案，以防像女权主义者，甚至更糟的共产主义者这样的人上了节目。

sentences.en: And that's why they invented bleeping or sort of bleeping.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们发明“哔”声，或者说类似“哔”声的原因。

sentences.en: The original bleep began as a music that cut in suddenly to a broadcast that might be sort of problematic.
sentences.zh: 最初的“哔”声始于突然切入广播的音乐，用来掩盖可能存在问题的片段。

sentences.en: They had another operator the entire time playing classical music.
sentences.zh: 他们全程安排了另一名操作员播放古典音乐。

sentences.en: And if anything came up that they didn't want to hear, there would be a signal to this engineer.
sentences.zh: 如果出现了他们不想听到的内容，就会给这位工程师发信号。

sentences.en: And like, boom, you'd be hearing classical music that second.
sentences.zh: 然后，砰的一声，你那一秒听到的就是古典音乐了。

sentences.en: That was like the original version of bleeping.
sentences.zh: 那就像是“哔”声的原始版本。

sentences.en: The classical music solution was widely adopted by radio stations across the United States shortly after the Petrova incident.
sentences.zh: 在彼得罗娃事件后不久，古典音乐解决方案就被美国各地的广播电台广泛采用。

sentences.en: In fact, Olga Petrova ran into the censorship regime in 1924 when she read from one of her plays on a different station.
sentences.zh: 事实上，奥尔加·彼得罗娃在1924年又遇到了审查制度，当时她在另一个电台朗读她的一部剧作。

sentences.en: This time, when she hit the potentially offensive material, it didn't get on air.
sentences.zh: 这一次，当她触及潜在的冒犯性内容时，它没能播出。

sentences.en: There was an old woman who lived in a shoe.
sentences.zh: 有个老妇人住在鞋子里。

sentences.en: She had so many children.
sentences.zh: 她生了太多孩子。

sentences.en: By the 1950s, radio had gone fully professional with big national broadcasters reaching everyone in America.
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪50年代，广播已经完全专业化，大型全国性广播公司覆盖了全美每个人。

sentences.en: And it was joined by a dynamic upstart flash-in-the-pan invention called television.
sentences.zh: 随后，一项充满活力的、昙花一现的新发明——电视——也加入了进来。

sentences.en: Heard of it?
sentences.zh: 听说过吗？

sentences.en: By this point, radio and TV were regulated by the Federal Communications Commission,
sentences.zh: 到那时，广播和电视都受到联邦通信委员会（FCC）的监管，

sentences.en: who had the power to dish out fines and even revoke licenses for any content they found indecent.
sentences.zh: 他们有权对任何被认为不雅的内容处以罚款，甚至吊销执照。

sentences.en: And it was into this brave new world that the bleep button was born.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个勇敢的新世界里，消音键诞生了。

sentences.en: The first bleep was created so radio stations could cover up swear words just in the nick of time.
sentences.zh: 第一个“哔”声的诞生，是为了让广播电台能及时掩盖脏话。

sentences.en: Most live radio isn't actually live.
sentences.zh: 大多数直播广播其实并不是真正的实时直播。

sentences.en: It's sent to the airwaves seven seconds after it happens in real life.
sentences.zh: 它会在现实发生七秒后才通过电波发送出去。

sentences.en: This gives broadcasters seven seconds to catch a swear word and cover it up with a bleep sound before it reaches your ears.
sentences.zh: 这给了广播公司七秒钟的时间来捕捉脏话，并在它传到你耳朵之前用“哔”声掩盖它。

sentences.en: You've got a producer with his finger on the button, and the button disconnects the broadcast audio and goes eeep.
sentences.zh: 你有一个手指放在按钮上的制作人，这个按钮会切断广播音频并发出“哔”的一声。

sentences.en: I could probably do that better if I worked on it.
sentences.zh: 如果我练习一下，我可能做得更好。

sentences.en: I don't need to.
sentences.zh: 我不需要。

sentences.en: That's Richard Factor.
sentences.zh: 那是理查德·法克特（Richard Factor）。

sentences.en: He was a board operator at WABC in New York in the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 他在20世纪60年代是纽约 WABC 电台的控制台操作员。

sentences.en: Back in the day, it was like the biggest radio station in the country, possibly in the world.
sentences.zh: 在当时，那可是全国，甚至可能是全世界最大的广播电台。

sentences.en: Richard says the reason the bleep was an obvious choice is because radio stations use something called an oscillator.
sentences.zh: 理查德说，“哔”声之所以成为显而易见的选择，是因为广播电台使用一种叫振荡器的东西。

sentences.en: An oscillator is built into most mixing boards, and it sends out test tones like 100 hertz or 500 hertz or bleep the 1 kilohertz tone.
sentences.zh: 大多数混音台上都内置了振荡器，它会发出测试音，比如100赫兹、500赫兹，或者“哔”的一声1千赫兹音调。

sentences.en: It creates a tone.
sentences.zh: 它能产生一种音调。

sentences.en: It's like a synthesizer.
sentences.zh: 就像合成器一样。

sentences.en: If you have a synthesizer, it's nothing but an audio oscillator that they filter and make different tones out of it.
sentences.zh: 如果你有合成器，它本质上就是一个音频振荡器，通过过滤产生不同的音调。

sentences.en: Since the oscillator was already built in, Richard says using the bleep tone to cover up a swear word, well, it just made sense.
sentences.zh: 既然振荡器是内置的，理查德说，用“哔”声来掩盖脏话，嗯，这很合理。

sentences.en: There's nothing special about it.
sentences.zh: 它没什么特别的。

sentences.en: It just covered up the naughty audio.
sentences.zh: 它只是掩盖了不雅的音频。

sentences.en: Because the alternative was just a long stretch of nothing.
sentences.zh: 因为唯一的替代方案就是长长的一段空白。

sentences.en: And silence on the radio is a total no-go.
sentences.zh: 而广播中出现静音是绝对不行的。

sentences.en: You have to have something, because if you go off the air for seven seconds, somebody tunes in another station.
sentences.zh: 你必须得有声音，因为如果你断播七秒钟，别人就会换台了。

sentences.en: While the bleep tone was kicking around in the 50s, it became ubiquitous much later, thanks in part to a fateful Supreme Court case.
sentences.zh: 虽然“哔”声在50年代就已经存在，但它后来变得无处不在，部分归功于一起重大的最高法院案件。

sentences.en: In 1973, the radio station WBAI decided to test the waters and see if America was ready for uncensored content.
sentences.zh: 1973年，WBAI 广播电台决定试水，看看美国是否准备好接受未经审查的内容。

sentences.en: They aired a long clip from a comedy routine by George Carlin called The Seven Words You Can Never Say on Television.
sentences.zh: 他们播放了乔治·卡林（George Carlin）的一段喜剧表演片段，名为《你永远不能在电视上说的七个词》。

sentences.en: For those wondering, the words are, and of course, the routine was uncensored, and it had a ton of curse words.
sentences.zh: 对于那些好奇的人，这七个词是……当然，这段表演未经审查，里面有大量的脏话。

sentences.en: So the FCC sent a warning to the station's parent company, Pacifica.
sentences.zh: 于是 FCC 向该电台的母公司太平洋广播电台（Pacifica）发出了警告。

sentences.en: The whole thing became a First Amendment case at the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 整件事最终演变成了一起最高法院的宪法第一修正案案件。

sentences.en: And the court ruled that, actually, no, you cannot air all those swear words.
sentences.zh: 法院裁定，实际上，不，你不能播出所有那些脏话。

sentences.en: And, yeah, the FCC did have the right to decide what was and was not appropriate for the airwaves.
sentences.zh: 而且，是的，FCC 确实有权决定什么适合广播，什么不适合。

sentences.en: The ruling emboldened the FCC, who gave out bigger and bigger fines.
sentences.zh: 这一裁决助长了 FCC 的气焰，他们开出了越来越大的罚单。

sentences.en: By 2006, Congress passed a law instructing the FCC to issue fines of $325,000 for broadcasting swear words on radio and TV.
sentences.zh: 到2006年，国会通过了一项法律，指示 FCC 对在广播和电视上播出脏话的行为处以325,000美元的罚款。

sentences.en: With all of that going on, the bleep sensor became more and more popular.
sentences.zh: 随着这一切的发生，“哔”声传感器变得越来越流行。

sentences.en: People wanted edgier content, stuff that felt more like real life.
sentences.zh: 人们想要更前卫的内容，更像真实生活的东西。

sentences.en: And at the same time, the FCC was going fine crazy.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，FCC 变得疯狂地开罚单。

sentences.en: So the bleep was a perfect solution.
sentences.zh: 所以“哔”声是一个完美的解决方案。

sentences.en: In part because the bleep doesn't just erase a bad word, it also draws attention to it.
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于，“哔”声不仅抹去了脏话，还引起了人们对它的注意。

sentences.en: The bleep, I think, is good insofar as it announces we are messing with what it is that we're showing you.
sentences.zh: 我认为“哔”声之所以好，是因为它宣告了我们正在对所展示的内容进行干预。

sentences.en: Robert Thompson is a professor of media history at Syracuse University.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·汤普森（Robert Thompson）是雪城大学的媒体历史学教授。

sentences.en: What you are about to see is not happening the way it actually happened.
sentences.zh: 你即将看到的内容并不是按它实际发生的方式呈现的。

sentences.en: It's been changed.
sentences.zh: 它被修改过了。

sentences.en: And we've got this obvious beep that warns you of that.
sentences.zh: 我们用这个明显的“哔”声来提醒你这一点。

sentences.en: And bleeps throughout our life are generally warnings.
sentences.zh: 而且我们生活中的“哔”声通常都是警告。

sentences.en: If a garbage truck is backing up toward you, you hear the bleeps to warn you.
sentences.zh: 如果垃圾车正倒车向你驶来，你会听到“哔”声来警告你。

sentences.en: Before a weather advisory comes up on your television set, we hear those annoying beeps.
sentences.zh: 在电视上出现天气预报之前，我们也会听到那些恼人的“哔”声。

sentences.en: The bleep sound became popular in part because it is obnoxious.
sentences.zh: “哔”声之所以流行，部分原因在于它很讨厌。

sentences.en: It feels kind of illicit, even while it is technically covering up the swear word.
sentences.zh: 它让人感觉有点非法，尽管从技术上讲它只是在掩盖脏话。

sentences.en: The bleep, in my opinion, actually emphasizes, it underlines, it foregrounds it.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，“哔”声实际上是在强调、加粗、凸显它。

sentences.en: By the early 2000s, the bleep was everywhere.
sentences.zh: 到了21世纪初，“哔”声已经无处不在。

sentences.en: The Jerry Springer Show made it a mainstay of daytime TV,
sentences.zh: 《杰瑞·斯普林格秀》（The Jerry Springer Show）使其成为日间电视的中流砥柱，

sentences.en: while reality shows like The Bachelor made it a staple in primetime.
sentences.zh: 而像《单身汉》这样的真人秀则使其成为黄金时段的常客。

sentences.en: And TV censors became more loosey-goosey in how they used the bleep.
sentences.zh: 电视审查员在使用“哔”声时也变得越来越随意。

sentences.en: If you listen to a bleep, a smart bleeper can often get the bleep begin after the first consonant of the word
sentences.zh: 如果你仔细听，一个聪明的消音员通常会让“哔”声在单词的第一个辅音之后开始，

sentences.en: and end before the last consonant of the word.
sentences.zh: 并在单词的最后一个辅音之前结束。

sentences.en: Everybody knows what they're saying.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道他们在说什么。

sentences.en: Lip reading will usually do it in itself.
sentences.zh: 读唇语通常就能看出来。

sentences.en: The advocacy group, the Parents Television and Media Council, did a study in the early 2000s
sentences.zh: 倡导组织“家长电视与媒体委员会”（Parents Television and Media Council）在21世纪初做了一项研究，

sentences.en: and found that bleeping increased by, please don't laugh, 69% during a five-year period.
sentences.zh: 发现消音的使用在五年内增加了——请别笑——69%。

sentences.en: Reality TV was a big driver of this increase in bleeps.
sentences.zh: 真人秀电视节目是这种“哔”声增加的主要推手。

sentences.en: But there's another reason it really took off in the early 2000s.
sentences.zh: 但它在21世纪初真正流行起来还有另一个原因。

sentences.en: It's the rise of what Maria Bustillos calls the comedic meta-bleep.
sentences.zh: 那就是玛丽亚·布斯蒂略斯（Maria Bustillos）所说的“喜剧元消音”的兴起。

sentences.en: The moments when a comedy show uses the bleep not to cover up a swear word,
sentences.zh: 喜剧节目使用“哔”声的时刻，不是为了掩盖脏话，

sentences.en: but as a punchline in and of itself.
sentences.zh: 而是将其本身作为笑点。

sentences.en: It's like the strange signal for every viewer of like,
sentences.zh: 这就像是给每位观众发出的奇怪信号，仿佛在说：

sentences.en: we're going to break into your fictive dream now
sentences.zh: 我们现在要闯入你们的虚构梦境，

sentences.en: and introduce the concept of naughtiness or indecency.
sentences.zh: 并引入“淘气”或“不雅”的概念。

sentences.en: A bleep is like a rimshot after a joke.
sentences.zh: “哔”声就像笑话讲完后的鼓点声。

sentences.en: If you didn't hear that bad word, we bleeped it
sentences.zh: 如果你没听清那个脏话，我们把它消音了，

sentences.en: so you could be sure that you knew where it was.
sentences.zh: 这样你就能确定它原本在哪里。

sentences.en: The idea of the comedy bleep is actually pretty old.
sentences.zh: 喜剧消音的想法其实由来已久。

sentences.en: Comedian Jack Parr did a version of the joke in the 1960s,
sentences.zh: 喜剧演员杰克·帕尔（Jack Parr）在20世纪60年代就做过一个类似的笑话版本，

sentences.en: replacing words in famous advertisements with a cuckoo clock sound.
sentences.zh: 用布谷鸟钟的声音替换了著名广告中的词汇。

sentences.en: Mother, please, I'd rather...
sentences.zh: 妈妈，求你了，我宁愿……

sentences.en: Myself.
sentences.zh: 我自己来。

sentences.en: What's wrong, Helen?
sentences.zh: 怎么了，海伦？

sentences.en: Maybe it's your...
sentences.zh: 也许是因为你的……

sentences.en: The toothpaste for people who can't always...
sentences.zh: 这款牙膏专为那些无法时刻……的人准备。

sentences.en: Between meals.
sentences.zh: 在两餐之间（刷牙）。

sentences.en: In the early 2000s, it became a standard type of joke,
sentences.zh: 在21世纪初，这成了一种标准的笑话类型，

sentences.en: where the bleep button is used so much, it sounds absurd.
sentences.zh: 消音键被频繁使用，以至于听起来荒谬可笑。

sentences.en: My favorite example of this was the Osborns, starting in, what was it, 2002.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的例子是《奥斯本一家》（The Osbournes），始于2002年左右。

sentences.en: Way funnier to watch that show as it aired with the bleeps
sentences.zh: 看那档节目首播时带消音的版本，

sentences.en: than to play it on DVD or finding it on streaming without the bleeps.
sentences.zh: 比看DVD或在流媒体上找无消音版要有趣得多。

sentences.en: The bleeps had almost a Morse code telegraphic kind of rhythm and music to it.
sentences.zh: 这些消音声几乎有一种摩尔斯电码般的节奏感和音乐性。

sentences.en: I'm sick and tired of...
sentences.zh: 我真是受够了……

sentences.en: Profanity as poetry, courtesy of the bleep.
sentences.zh: 以消音为媒介的脏话诗学。

sentences.en: Every word I go, this...
sentences.zh: 我每走一步，这……

sentences.en: It's driving me...
sentences.zh: 这简直让我……

sentences.en: One of my favorite ones was the Writers of Arrested Development.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的例子之一来自《发展受阻》（Arrested Development）的编剧们。

sentences.en: There's an Arrested Development episode where they're bleeping all the way through the scene,
sentences.zh: 《发展受阻》里有一集，他们整场戏都在消音，

sentences.en: and nobody can tell exactly what they were saying.
sentences.zh: 没人能听出他们到底在说什么。

sentences.en: You know, I'm in pretty good shape.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的状态相当不错。

sentences.en: You could be eating my dust all day, slowpoke.
sentences.zh: 你整天都只能吃我的灰，慢吞吞的家伙。

sentences.en: And you might be eating...
sentences.zh: 而你可能会吃……

sentences.en: That's gonna...
sentences.zh: 那会……

sentences.en: Well, let's hope it doesn't come to that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，希望事情不会发展到那一步。

sentences.en: The show's creator, Mitch Hurwitz, says his actors weren't actually swearing during these sequences.
sentences.zh: 该剧主创米奇·赫维兹（Mitch Hurwitz）表示，演员在拍摄这些片段时其实并没有真的在骂人。

sentences.en: They would say the words, lip flap.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在对口型。

sentences.en: So if somebody read their lips, they wouldn't be able to tell what swear word it was supposed to be.
sentences.zh: 所以如果有人读唇语，也无法分辨出原本应该是哪个脏话。

sentences.en: Hurwitz explained the joke's appeal to NPR.
sentences.zh: 赫维兹向美国国家公共电台（NPR）解释了这个笑话的吸引力。

sentences.en: That was the point at which we realized, you know, it's more fun to not know exactly what it is that we're saying.
sentences.zh: 就在那时我们意识到，不知道我们到底在说什么反而更有趣。

sentences.en: It becomes kind of a puzzle for people.
sentences.zh: 这对观众来说变成了一种谜题。

sentences.en: And I think it's about, you know, letting your imagination do the work.
sentences.zh: 我认为这在于让你的想象力去发挥作用。

sentences.en: The apotheosis of this trend is a recurring sketch on Jimmy Kimmel's late-night show.
sentences.zh: 这种趋势的巅峰是吉米·坎摩尔（Jimmy Kimmel）深夜秀中的一个常驻环节。

sentences.en: It's called Unnecessary Centorship, where he replaces parts of perfectly normal sentences with long, obnoxious bleeps.
sentences.zh: 它叫“不必要的审查”，他用刺耳的长消音声替换了正常句子中的部分词汇。

sentences.en: President Obama delivered his final State of the Union address and urged Americans to build a, quote, big-f***ing nation.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马总统发表了最后一次国情咨文，并敦促美国人建立一个，引用他的话，“伟大的他妈的国家”。

sentences.en: We built a space program almost overnight, and 12 years later, we were f***ing on the moon.
sentences.zh: 我们几乎在一夜之间建立了太空计划，12年后，我们就他妈的登上了月球。

sentences.en: In so many ways, the censor bleep noise is like a super-swear.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，消音声就像是一种“超级脏话”。

sentences.en: It can be used to barely conceal a swear word, like on Jerry Springer.
sentences.zh: 它既可以用来勉强掩盖脏话，比如在《杰瑞·斯普林格秀》里。

sentences.en: Or it can be used to let our minds run wild and consider all sorts of possibilities, like arrested development.
sentences.zh: 也可以用来让我们的思维天马行空，考虑各种可能性，比如在《发展受阻》里。

sentences.en: As a tool of censorship, it's not that effective.
sentences.zh: 作为一种审查工具，它其实并不那么有效。

sentences.en: Which is why certain political action groups would like to see it dead.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么某些政治行动团体希望它消失。

sentences.en: Hello, Tim.
sentences.zh: 你好，蒂姆。

sentences.en: Can you hear me, Chris?
sentences.zh: 你能听到我说话吗，克里斯？

sentences.en: Tim Winter is the head of the Parents Television and Media Council.
sentences.zh: 蒂姆·温特（Tim Winter）是家长电视与媒体委员会（PTC）的负责人。

sentences.en: We are a grassroots, non-profit, non-partisan organization.
sentences.zh: 我们是一个草根、非营利、无党派的组织。

sentences.en: Our mission is to protect children from the graphic sex, violence, and profanity that seems so pervasive in our entertainment media today.
sentences.zh: 我们的使命是保护儿童免受当今娱乐媒体中无处不在的露骨性、暴力和脏话的影响。

sentences.en: The PTC is famous for having monitors watch broadcast TV and submit complaints to the Federal Communications Commission.
sentences.zh: PTC以让监督员观看广播电视并向联邦通信委员会（FCC）提交投诉而闻名。

sentences.en: They also do things like lobbying Congress to increase the fines against broadcasters who put swearing on the air.
sentences.zh: 他们还做一些游说国会的工作，以增加对在广播中播放脏话的广播公司的罚款。

sentences.en: The PTC believes TV and radio should be a family-friendly haven, where content is appropriate for everyone.
sentences.zh: PTC认为电视和广播应该是一个适合家庭的避风港，内容应适合所有人。

sentences.en: And for Tim, that conviction has created a complicated relationship with bleeping.
sentences.zh: 对蒂姆来说，这种信念让他与消音产生了复杂的关系。

sentences.en: First and foremost, when it comes to a bleep button versus hearing the profanity,
sentences.zh: 首先，当谈到消音键与直接听到脏话时，

sentences.en: especially on entertainment content that is likely to be consumed by children,
sentences.zh: 特别是在儿童可能会接触的娱乐内容中，

sentences.en: the bleep button is better than the profanity, usually, generally speaking, in our opinion.
sentences.zh: 在我们看来，消音键通常比直接听到脏话要好。

sentences.en: And it's one of those things where we don't want to let perfect be the enemy of good.
sentences.zh: 我们不想让“完美”成为“优秀”的敌人。

sentences.en: But still, he thinks the bleep button isn't some neutral thing.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，他认为消音键并非中立之物。

sentences.en: In Tim's mind, the bleep button is kind of like cheating.
sentences.zh: 在蒂姆看来，消音键有点像作弊。

sentences.en: If the intention is to shock, then he put the loud bleep in there.
sentences.zh: 如果目的是为了制造冲击，那么他们就放进那个响亮的消音声。

sentences.en: And that's exactly what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 而这正是他们所做的。

sentences.en: They're doing it for effect.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做是为了效果。

sentences.en: This is no earnest effort to make sure that the program doesn't violate indecency standards.
sentences.zh: 这绝不是为了确保节目不违反不雅标准而做出的真诚努力。

sentences.en: This is a way to almost do the opposite.
sentences.zh: 这反而是一种反其道而行之的方式。

sentences.en: You're doing it intentionally to suggest and to provoke.
sentences.zh: 你是故意这样做来暗示和挑衅的。

sentences.en: You're almost adding it back in and adding emphasis to it, even though you're not saying the words.
sentences.zh: 你几乎是在把它加回去并加以强调，尽管你并没有说出那个词。

sentences.en: In 2010, the PTC launched a boycott against a sitcom based on a Twitter account called
sentences.zh: 2010年，PTC发起了一场抵制活动，针对一部基于Twitter账号的喜剧，名字叫

sentences.en: The Twitter thread used a profanity in the title, but the show didn't.
sentences.zh: 那个Twitter账号在标题里用了脏话，但剧名没有。

sentences.en: And in the trailers, they actually just used the word bleep.
sentences.zh: 在预告片里，他们实际上直接用了“哔”这个词。

sentences.en: Bleep my dad says.
sentences.zh: 《我老爸说的话》（$#*! My Dad Says）。

sentences.en: Thursdays this fall, only CBS.
sentences.zh: 今年秋季每周四，仅在CBS播出。

sentences.en: They called sponsors of Bleep my dad says and told them to boycott the show.
sentences.zh: 他们联系了《我老爸说的话》的赞助商，要求他们抵制该剧。

sentences.en: It was canceled after a few episodes, mostly because nobody was really watching.
sentences.zh: 该剧在几集后就被取消了，主要是因为根本没人看。

sentences.en: The bleep button might be on its way out, but not for the protect the children reasons favored by Tim Winter and the PTC.
sentences.zh: 消音键可能正走向淘汰，但不是因为蒂姆·温特和PTC所主张的“保护儿童”的原因。

sentences.en: It's because swearing across society has become more and more accepted.
sentences.zh: 这是因为整个社会对脏话的接受度越来越高了。

sentences.en: A Reuters poll found that only 14 percent of Americans never swear in day-to-day life.
sentences.zh: 路透社的一项民意调查发现，只有14%的美国人在日常生活中从不说脏话。

sentences.en: Recently, the FCC has lost some of its regulatory power.
sentences.zh: 最近，FCC失去了一些监管权力。

sentences.en: In 2010, the Second Circuit Court of Appeals struck down the FCC's right to levy fines for fleeting swear words in live broadcast,
sentences.zh: 2010年，第二巡回上诉法院推翻了FCC对直播中转瞬即逝的脏话进行罚款的权利，

sentences.en: saying their rules were, quote, unconstitutionally vague.
sentences.zh: 称其规则“违宪且模糊不清”。

sentences.en: In the years since that ruling, TV and radio hasn't been a vulgarity free-for-all.
sentences.zh: 在那项裁决后的几年里，电视和广播并没有变成粗俗的无政府状态。

sentences.en: Advertisers and parents probably wouldn't abide that.
sentences.zh: 广告商和家长们可能不会容忍那样。

sentences.en: But the standards are definitely changing.
sentences.zh: 但标准确实在改变。

sentences.en: Most stations don't bleep words like bitch or ass anymore.
sentences.zh: 大多数电台不再对“bitch”或“ass”之类的词进行消音了。

sentences.en: It's possible we're heading towards a world where
sentences.zh: 我们可能正走向一个世界，

sentences.en: and won't be out.
sentences.zh: 而不会被消音。

sentences.en: But personally, I hope we keep the bleep.
sentences.zh: 但我个人希望我们保留消音键。

sentences.en: The bleep button is America's superego.
sentences.zh: 消音键是美国的“超我”。

sentences.en: It's the desire to say exactly what we want all the time and the knowledge that we can't.
sentences.zh: 它代表了我们时刻想畅所欲言的欲望，以及我们深知自己无法做到的现实。

sentences.en: When we come back, the delicate art of censoring swear words during live broadcasts.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将探讨直播中审查脏话的精妙艺术。

sentences.en: I'm ready to press the big red button.
sentences.zh: 我准备好按下那个红色大按钮了。

sentences.en: Because at this point, I'm like, oh, if this goes over the air, a station's going to get fined.
sentences.zh: 因为到了这一步，我在想，噢，如果这播出去，电台会被罚款的。

sentences.en: My whole career is over.
sentences.zh: 我的整个职业生涯就完了。

sentences.en: More with Chris Berube after this.
sentences.zh: 稍后继续收听克里斯·贝鲁比（Chris Berube）的节目。

sentences.en: Today, when you hear the bleep button on radio and TV,
sentences.zh: 今天，当你在广播和电视上听到消音键时，

sentences.en: it's almost always in pre-recorded content, like a reality TV show or a sitcom.
sentences.zh: 它几乎总是出现在预录内容中，比如真人秀或情景喜剧。

sentences.en: But it's rarely used in live broadcaSt.
sentences.zh: 但在直播中却很少使用。

sentences.zh: 想想看，你见过多少次直播中出现严重失误的情况。

sentences.zh: 比如威尔·史密斯在奥斯卡颁奖礼上打了克里斯·洛克，

sentences.zh: 然后他开始大喊大叫。

sentences.en: And they just cut off his sound.
sentences.zh: 他们直接切断了他的声音。

sentences.en: Same thing any time a professional athlete loses their cool.
sentences.zh: 任何职业运动员失去冷静时也是一样。

sentences.en: LeBron James eventually was carried to the heat bench.
sentences.zh: 勒布朗·詹姆斯最终被抬到了热火队的替补席上。

sentences.zh: 我们正在尝试获取最新消息。

sentences.en: This is cramps, Mike.
sentences.zh: 这是抽筋，迈克。

sentences.en: They're trying to get him.
sentences.zh: 他们正在尝试帮他。

sentences.en: Silence works just fine as a replacement for a bad word on television.
sentences.zh: 在电视上，静音完全可以作为脏话的替代品。

sentences.en: Because there are still images being broadcaSt.
sentences.zh: 因为屏幕上还有图像在播放。

sentences.en: But on the radio, silence doesn't cut it.
sentences.zh: 但在广播里，静音可不行。

sentences.en: People think silence is dead air.
sentences.zh: 人们会以为静音就是死寂。

sentences.en: For years, live radio used the bleep sound effect.
sentences.zh: 多年来，直播广播一直使用“哔”声特效。

sentences.zh: 但他们在20世纪70年代停止了使用。

sentences.zh: 这归功于一位非常讨厌消音键的导播。

sentences.zh: 大多数时候，你根本不需要消音。

sentences.en: Which, again, you know, you're calling it a bleep only because you got to call it something.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，你叫它“哔”声只是因为你得给它起个名字。

sentences.en: It's really just a tone to fill dead air while the naughtiness went away.
sentences.zh: 它其实只是一个用来填补死寂的音调，同时把那些淘气的词过滤掉。

sentences.zh: 那是理查德·法克特（Richard Factor）。
